layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 15 congressional districts — the largest districts Ohio carries below the state itself, larger on average than its 33 Senate districts

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 15 features for Ohio, measured 2026-11-11. These are the districts the current members were elected from in 2024. TIGERweb's layer 0 carries the map for the 120th Congress, whose members were elected on 3 November 2026 and take office on 3 January 2027; measured that day, 13 of the 15 districts differ between the two maps, and the builder refuses to write layer 4 on or after that date. Simplified together with the two state legislative maps, by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Ohio Senate District
layers.rank_note: 33 Senate districts — smaller on average than a congressional district; each is three whole House districts

source.answers: The Ohio Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 33 features, measured 2026-11-11. Ohio's constitution builds each Senate district from three whole House districts, so the Senate and House maps are simplified in one run and the build refuses unless every Senate line lies exactly on its three House districts. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: oh-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Senate's own site (ohiosenate.gov): the senator's name and party from the Senate's member directory, and the Statehouse office and telephone from each senator's own page, as that page prints them. A seat the directory lists as vacant says so.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 88 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer, larger on average than a House district

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 88 features, measured 2026-11-11. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Ohio county is governed by an elected board of three county commissioners, except Cuyahoga and Summit, whose charters set up an elected county executive and county council, and elects officers such as an auditor, a treasurer, a prosecuting attorney, a sheriff, a clerk of courts, a recorder, an engineer and a coroner; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap oh-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 612 school districts, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 612 features for Ohio, measured 2026-11-11: the state's city, local and exempted village school districts. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Ohio, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each school district is governed by a board of education, and no list of the members was read in this pass — recorded as gap oh-school-board-members.

layers.label: Ohio House District
layers.rank_note: 99 House districts — three in each Senate district, and smaller on average than a county

source.answers: The Ohio House district covering the point, and the member holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 99 features, measured 2026-11-11. Simplified in one run with the Senate map, so the three House districts under each Senate district share its lines exactly, by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: oh-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the House's own site (ohiohouse.gov): the member's name and party from the House's member directory, and the Statehouse office and telephone from each member's own page, as that page prints them. The House links an e-mail form for each member rather than printing an address, so none is shown. A seat the directory lists as vacant says so.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,233 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside Ohio (1,744 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Ohio (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='39'. 1,744 features in the app's box, which reaches into Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky, West Virginia and Pennsylvania, 1,233 of them inside Ohio and kept in the archive, measured 2026-11-11.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Ohio. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Village
layers.rank_note: 923 incorporated cities and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 923 features for Ohio, measured 2026-11-11: 253 cities and 670 villages, all but one village recorded as an active government (the card says so for that one). MOST OF OHIO IS IN NO CITY OR VILLAGE (9.6% of its land, 10,137.6 of 105,824.6 km2, is inside one), and there the township and the county are the local governments, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Ohio's 1,300-odd townships are not drawn yet (recorded as gap oh-townships), and the Census's census-designated places are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Ohio's mayors and council members has been read for this app, so the card names no one rather than guessing. Recorded as gap oh-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-11: 968 points in Ohio's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Ohio — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Ohio Statehouse, 1 Capitol Square, Columbus, Franklin County. Measured 2026-11-11 against the shipped files: 363 m inside its congressional district, 442 m inside its Senate and House districts.

negative_point.note: Leamington, Ontario, on the Canadian shore of Lake Erie — outside Ohio and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11: TIGERweb's state layer places it in no state (control: the Ohio Statehouse returns Ohio), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and none of the 25 outlines in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS IN CANADA, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Ohio outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (88 counties).
The 88 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 15 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), the map the sitting members were elected from in 2024, drawn until 3 January 2027.
The 33 Ohio Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), simplified in one run with the House map so each Senate line lies exactly on its three House districts.
The 99 Ohio House districts, TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Ohio elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from oh/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
